confirmed_issues.quote_a: bleaching is a chemical action of a basic substance
confirmed_issues.problem: This says bleach removes colour because it is basic. Household bleach removes colour because sodium hypochlorite oxidises the coloured substance. Being basic is not the cause: other bases, such as sodium hydroxide or the antacid, do not bleach. Learners would take away a wrong cause-and-effect link.
confirmed_issues.correct_value: Bleaching is a chemical (oxidation) process in which sodium hypochlorite in bleach changes a coloured substance into a colourless one; liquid bleach also happens to be basic (pH about 11).
confirmed_issues.reference: Household bleach (sodium hypochlorite) bleaches by oxidation; it is basic but basicity is not the cause.

confirmed_issues.quote_a: Acids release hydrogen ions (H+) and bases release hydroxide ions (OH-), which explains the pH colours, the fizzing, Juma's antacid relief and the behaviour of salts in air
confirmed_issues.problem: The behaviour of salts in air cannot be explained by H+ and OH- ions. Hygroscopic, deliquescent and efflorescent behaviour depends on a salt taking in water vapour or losing water of crystallisation, as Lesson 6 teaches. It has nothing to do with releasing H+ or OH-.
confirmed_issues.correct_value: H+ and OH- explain the pH colours, the acid reactions and neutralisation. The damp salt and crumbling washing soda are explained by salts taking in water vapour (hygroscopic/deliquescent) or losing water of crystallisation (efflorescent).
